clue.text: Contemplates terminal near Enfield?

parts.note: to contemplate is to ponder, here in the third person
a terminal is an end point

explanation.surface: Someone muses over a railway or bus terminus somewhere north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Ponders End is a district of north London right beside Enfield, so the question mark flags a definition by location.
explanation.definitionFit: The district lies in the London borough of Enfield, so a place near Enfield describes it by example.

clue.text: Reckoned to be under pressure in such a cell?

indicators.note: in a down clue the reckoned word sits below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
to reckon a sum is to add it up

explanation.surface: A question about a prisoner judged to be under strain in a particular kind of cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be under' places ADDED below P in the down light. A padded cell is the cushioned room in an asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned asylum room is called a padded cell, so the adjective describes that sort of cell.

clue.text: No copper coins in returning from Japan

indicators.note: returning means the whole run of pieces is read back to front

parts.note: taken as written
P is a penny, so PP stands for pennies, copper coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone back from Japan without any small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NO + PP + IN (NOPPIN) end to end; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippon is the Japanese people's own name for their country.

clue.text: Shopkeeper shutting the door on one, possibly

definitions.text: Shopkeeper shutting the door on one, possibly

parts.words: Shopkeeper shutting the door on one, possibly
parts.note: a trader locking up at one o'clock rather than one customer: the weekly half-day when shops shut in the afternoon

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper slams the door in a customer's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' seems to be a person but is the time, one o'clock; British towns once had a weekly half-day when shops shut at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional British half-day saw shops locking up at lunchtime, so a trader shutting at one o'clock illustrates it.

clue.text: Amount to nothing, wrestling

parts.note: a sum is an amount
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Wrestling comes to nothing, says a sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling between heavyweights.

clue.text: Novel not in fashion, like "A Farewell to Arms"?

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or form, so these letters are moulded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous war novel is no longer trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a nod to Hemingway's book, and 'in fashion' a phrase, but 'fashion' rearranges NOVEL NOT IN; the title is read literally as giving up weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidding farewell to arms means laying down weapons, which is a pacifist, peaceable stance.

clue.text: Achievements of Book V

definitions.meaning: the fifth book of the New Testament, after the four Gospels

explanation.surface: The accomplishments recorded in the fifth volume of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds are things done, and the Bible's fifth New Testament book tells of the apostles' deeds.

clue.text: Like a peak with no internal cold-that describes the weather

indicators.note: with no internal says a letter is dropped from inside the word, not its ends

parts.note: climactic means forming a climax or high point
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A mountain-top free of chill, in a remark about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIMACTIC loses the C in its middle to leave the near twin that describes weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-run weather of a region.

clue.text: Pilot too old? A poor way to travel!

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
age is being old, as in 'with age'

explanation.surface: A passenger worries the captain is too elderly, then calls the trip a cheap and miserable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too' is a link meaning 'as well'. Steerage was the cheapest berth on an emigrant ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class on old passenger ships, cramped quarters for poor travellers.

clue.text: Carriage to expel fellows going to Tasmania, originally

parts.note: to deport someone is to expel them from a country
men are fellows

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Convicts are shipped off to Tasmania, as in the days of transportation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'going to' are links. The surface recalls British convicts transported to Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here means bearing or posture, the way one holds oneself.

clue.text: You and I embracing conditional partner

indicators.note: embracing means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: you and I together are we
if is the conditional conjunction

explanation.surface: Two people hug a partner whose commitment has conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a marriage partner, and the answer is the female one.

clue.text: Calling up? Went off topic in scorn

indicators.note: something that went off has broken up or exploded, so these letters scatter and regroup

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone digresses scornfully while discussing a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling up' suggests a phone call but means summoning recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: The draft summons civilians into compulsory military service, a call-up.

clue.text: Penny included in new money from Melbourne, for example

indicators.note: included in means the first piece is set inside the second
new means the word after it is made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A coin slipped in among fresh Australian currency from Melbourne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MONEY to EONYM, and P goes inside; 'from' is a link. Melbourne, Australia, takes its name from Lord Melbourne.
explanation.definitionFit: A name derived from a person qualifies: Melbourne's city name honours the Victorian prime minister.

clue.text: Sprinkling of soda ruin this old creature?

indicators.note: a sprinkling scatters things, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A dusting of soda wrecks a prehistoric animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' and the question mark simply link the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a prehistoric reptile, an extinct beast of great age.

clue.text: Opening of play on Virginia Hills, they start things off

parts.note: Act I is the opening part of a play
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A stage show premieres in the Virginia hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Activators set processes going, so they are what start things.

clue.text: Boycotting tipping on jet

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows on from the first

parts.note: jet is a deep black stone, so jet black
a ship that is listing is tipping to one side

explanation.surface: A remark about giving a tip on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipping' looks like gratuities and 'jet' like a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunning a firm or person by putting them on a banned roll is a form of boycott.

clue.text: A quiet generator is unmistakable

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a parent generates offspring

explanation.surface: A silent electrical generator is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generator' suggests a machine but means a parent, who begets children.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is evident or plain, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Old records of principal American composer

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy
Charles Ives was an American modernist composer

explanation.surface: The old recordings of a leading American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' suggests discs, but here means stored documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, old records kept for reference.

clue.text: New parson is heir to such people

indicators.note: new means the letters after it are made over into a different order

explanation.surface: The new vicar considers himself heir to his congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the definition looks back at the parson, whose flock is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson's flock are the people of his parish, the members of his congregation.

clue.text: Girls ordered English salmon

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Some girls order English salmon at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilse is a young salmon returning from the sea for the first time.

clue.text: Home of Trollope's law society

parts.note: the Bar is the legal profession of barristers
a set is a social group or circle

explanation.surface: A novelist's legal society, or where he lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Trollope's Barsetshire novels are set in an invented English county whose name shortens to this.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope's novels unfold in fictional Barsetshire, the county where his characters live.

clue.text: Inn the AA graded for this capital fellow

indicators.note: graded means sorted and arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation rates a pub, for the benefit of a visitor from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for this' links; the AA is the British motoring organisation that grades hotels and inns.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens, Greece's capital, is a man from that city.

clue.text: Ancient city's role in South Africa?

indicators.note: in means the role is placed inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Asking what part an old Greek city plays in modern South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful Greek city-state of the classical era.

clue.text: Brand of tie used by musician?

definitions.meaning: a stigma or insult that marks someone's name
a curved line in a score joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.surface: Which label of necktie does a musician wear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' and 'tie' look like clothing labels, not a slander and a curved mark in notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both an insult tarnishing a reputation and a notation curve binding notes legato.

clue.text: Sin of diplomat losing original order

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the diplomat word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent on a mission

indicators.note: original means only the opening letter of order is taken

explanation.surface: A diplomat's transgression costs him his first decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the O, from 'original order', out of ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Source of power seems, we hear, to be laid down ages ago

definitions.text: Source of power seems, we hear, to be laid down ages ago

parts.words: Source of power seems, we hear, to be laid down ages ago
parts.note: fuel deposits formed long ago, with seems sounding like seams, the layers that are mined

explanation.surface: An energy source appears to have been established long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seems, we hear' points to seams, the layers in which fossil fuel was laid down in prehistoric times.
explanation.definitionFit: These mining regions hold fossil fuel seams laid down in ancient times and burned for energy.

clue.text: Analysis of cricket-match

definitions.meaning: an examination or trial of something

explanation.surface: An expert dissects a cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination, and a Test is an international cricket fixture between national teams.

clue.text: Contracting organic tissue can be harsh

definitions.meaning: describing a substance that draws body tissue together

explanation.surface: Shrinking living tissue can be a cruel business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent lotion tightens skin and stops bleeding; figuratively it means severe or caustic.
